extracted.intended_audience: administrative agencies, public officials, regulated persons, and members of the public in Japan (actors implementing or affected by administrative procedures and public comment)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards under Japan's Administrative Procedure Act governing agency procedures for applications, adverse dispositions, administrative guidance, notifications, and especially public comment (notice-and-comment) when establishing Administrative Orders. Includes requirements for notice, hearings, publication, and consideration of submitted comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this Act is ... to improve fairness and transparency ... and thereby to promote the protection of the rights and interests of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the overall evaluative aim: procedures for dispositions, administrative guidance, notifications, and Administrative Orders must promote fairness/transparency (clarity in public understanding of content and decision-making).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key terms used in the Act (e.g., Laws and Regulations, Dispositions, Applications, Adverse Dispositions, Administrative Organs, Administrative Guidance, Notifications, Administrative Orders, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the operative meanings the rest of the Act uses; these definitions determine scope and applicability of procedural duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from Application (general categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters II to IV-2 do not apply to specified Dispositions and Administrative Guidance (e.g., Diet resolutions, judicial actions, prosecutorial actions, certain tax/financial enforcement, educational/training dispositions, prison accommodations, public officials' status dispositions, immigration/naturalization, exam-based dispositions, on-scene police acts, information-collection dispositions, administrative appeals, and procedures prescribed by other chapters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific categories of acts and actors exempted from the Act's procedural chapters; these exclusions are criteria for when notice/hearing/public-comment rules do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from Chapter VI (public comment) and other specific exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter VI (public comment) does not apply to certain Orders (e.g., Cabinet Orders about effective dates, pardons, Orders providing content of dispositions, designations, salaries/working conditions, or non-public review/disposition standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies types of Administrative Orders and circumstances where public comment procedures are not required; agencies must check these exemptions before implementing public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for national government organs and specified corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act does not apply to Dispositions and Administrative Guidance rendered towards national government organs or certain corporations designated by statute or Cabinet Order; Chapter VI exclusions likewise for certain administrative orders relating to government organization, personnel, budgets, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines limits of Act's reach vis-à-vis intra-governmental acts and supervision of special corporations; practical test for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Standards (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative agencies are to establish review standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must make review standards as concrete as possible given the nature of the permission, etc., and, except for extraordinary administrative inconvenience, must make them available to the public (posting at the office that receives Applications or other appropriate method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Period of Time for Processing (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative agencies must endeavor to establish standard periods of time typically needed between an Application's arrival and the rendering of a Disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where another organ receives Applications, the competent agency must also establish standard periods for transfer/processing; agencies must make standard periods public (posting at receiving office or other method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and Response to Applications (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon arrival of an Application, the agency must commence review without delay and either request amendments (with a considerable period to amend) or refuse permission when application fails to conform to pro forma requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must promptly act except for pro forma defects; specifies applicant amendment path vs refusal; emphasizes timely review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of Grounds for Refusal (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency refuses permission sought through an Application, it must concurrently show the grounds; where quantitative/objective standards make nonconformance clear, showing grounds on request may suffice; written dispositions must show grounds in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement to provide reasons protects transparency; exceptions allowed when objective indices make grounds obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Information to Applicants (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request, agencies must endeavor to indicate progress of review and prognosis for disposition; must endeavor to provide information concerning contents of written application, required attachments, and other filing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages agencies to assist applicants and increase transparency about process and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding of Public Hearings for Applications (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: When rendering Dispositions upon Applications where interests of persons other than applicants are to be considered, agencies must, where necessary, endeavor to provide opportunities for opinions of those persons (via public hearings or other methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should solicit affected third-party input where relevant to decisions on applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination Among Agencies (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Applications under review by other agencies do not excuse intentional delay; agencies concerned with the same application(s) should endeavor to accelerate review by coordinating and jointly hearing explanations where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates active inter-agency communication and avoidance of purposeful delay when multiple agencies are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition Standards (Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative agencies must endeavor to establish disposition standards and make them available to the public; standards should be as concrete as possible given the nature of the Adverse Disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to review standards: agencies should publish concrete standards used to judge adverse actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures Prerequisite for Adverse Dispositions (Article 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish procedures for hearing statements of opinion of persons who will become subject parties of Adverse Dispositions, categorizing when formal hearings are required vs when granting an opportunity for explanation suffices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies categories triggering hearings (rescission of permission, deprivation of qualification, dismissal of officers, appropriate other cases) and when opportunity to explain is enough; contains exceptions where immediate action is needed, where objective documents establish lack of qualifications, technical-measurement-based orders, monetary/funds dispositions, and Cabinet-ordered exceptions for insignificant duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of Grounds for Adverse Dispositions (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies render Adverse Dispositions, they must concurrently show the grounds to the subject parties unless there is a pressing need not to; if grounds are withheld for pressing need, they must be shown within a considerable period unless impossible; written dispositions must state grounds in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reasons accompany adverse actions, subject to narrow urgent exceptions, with later disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice Requirements for Formal Hearings (Article 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must give parties written notice well before hearings including: contents of the anticipated Adverse Disposition and legal provisions, facts causing the anticipated disposition, date/place of hearing, and name/location of the organization with jurisdiction over the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must also inform addressee they may appear and state opinion, produce documentary evidence or submit written statements in lieu of appearance, and that they may demand inspection of materials proving the facts until conclusion of the hearing; when addressee unknown, notice by posting on agency notice board suffices and is deemed reached two weeks after posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and Certification of Agents (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may appoint agents who can perform acts relating to hearings individually on behalf of parties; agents' status must be certified in writing; when an agent loses status the appointing party must notify the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits representation in hearings and requires written certification to establish agent authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervenors (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officials may request or permit persons not parties but recognized as having an interest to intervene; intervenors may appoint agents and agent rules apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism for interested third parties to participate in hearings when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of Records by Parties/Intervenors (Article 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties/intervenors whose interests would be harmed by the Adverse Disposition may request inspection of investigation results and other materials proving facts between notice and conclusion of hearing; agencies may not reject requests unless third-party interests would be harmed or other justifiable grounds exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows additional inspection requests arising during proceedings; agencies may set date/time/place for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidency Disqualifications (Article 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings are presided over by a designated official; specified persons (parties/intervenors, close relatives, agents, prior involved persons, guardians, or interested parties other than intervenors) may not preside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets conflict-of-interest and impartiality rules for presiding officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of Proceedings on Hearing Date (Article 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding official must at outset explain the contents of the anticipated Adverse Disposition, legal provisions, and facts; parties/intervenors may state opinions, produce evidence, submit questions with approval, appear with assistants, and be questioned by the presiding official; proceedings may continue despite absence of some parties and are ordinarily closed to the public unless agency deems otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies scope of participation, presiding official powers, and public access considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and Handling of Written Statements (Article 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties/intervenors may submit written statements and documentary evidence in lieu of appearing; presiding official may exhibit submitted materials to those appearing if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits non-appearance submissions and sharing of those materials at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting Continuation Dates (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If continuation is necessary, presiding official may assign continuation dates and must give written notice of date/location to parties/intervenors in advance (notification to those who appeared on prior date suffices in some cases); posting rules apply when locations are unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties have timely notice of continuity and the same posting/deemed receipt rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding Hearings with Nonappearance (Article 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding official may conclude hearing where parties fail to appear without justifiable grounds and have not submitted required written materials; in other nonappearance cases, official may ask for submission by due date and conclude when due date passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives presiding official discretion to conclude hearings when parties do not participate and sets steps for due-date requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of Hearings and Written Reports (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officials must prepare a record of proceedings showing outlines of parties' statements; records must be prepared on each hearing date and a written report with the presiding official's opinion on facts should be promptly submitted to the agency along with the record; parties/intervenors may demand inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents proceedings and provides agency with presiding official's assessment; inspection rights support transparency and potential challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening of Hearings (Article 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding official may reopen hearings under conditions provided in the Act (text indicates right to reopen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits reconsideration of proceedings when appropriate (details in Act context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions Following Hearings (Article 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements for agencies when rendering Adverse Dispositions after hearings, including showing grounds and following standards described elsewhere in the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow disposition standards and show grounds especially when hearings have occurred; ensures linkage between hearing record and final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations upon Requests for Review (Article 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies temporal or substantive limits on requests for review in relation to adverse dispositions (Act provides constraints and procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when and how affected persons can request review; safeguards against untimely or improper review requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Provisions for Hearings for Dismissal of Officers (Article 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Adverse Dispositions order dismissal of officers, special hearing provisions apply as prescribed in the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional procedural protections and/or requirements for serious employment-related adverse dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting of the Opportunity for Explanation (Article 29-31)
rubrics_metrics.description: When hearings are not required, agencies must provide the opportunity for explanation; Article 30 details methods of notice; Article 31 applies hearing procedures mutatis mutandis as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunity for explanation is a lower-formality procedural safeguard, and agencies should follow analogous procedures to hearings where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Principles of Administrative Guidance (Article 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets principles governing administrative guidance: guidance, recommendations, advice, or other acts by which an Administrative Organ seeks certain action/inaction without constituting Dispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative guidance must respect limits (not be a disposition) and agencies should adhere to general fairness/transparency principles when rendering guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Guidance for Applications (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies how administrative guidance relating to Applications should be conducted (e.g., advisory information about applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should assist applicants while respecting legal boundaries between guidance and dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Guidance for Authority over Permission (Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses administrative guidance in contexts where agencies have authority over permission decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance must not substitute for formal disposition; agencies should make clear distinctions and not mislead applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of Administrative Guidance (Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies acceptable means for rendering administrative guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should use appropriate, transparent channels for guidance and consider impacts when guidance is directed to many persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Guidance Directed to More Than One Person (Article 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: When guidance is intended for more than one person who meet certain conditions, agencies should standardize content (administrative guidance guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages publication/clarity when guidance has broad application, and provides basis for collective transparency and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Suspension of Administrative Guidance (Article 36-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for persons to request suspension of administrative guidance under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a procedural remedy when guidance improperly or unfairly burdens persons; agencies must consider such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Dispositions (Article 36-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes procedures for requesting formal dispositions (Article 36-3 placeholder referencing requests for dispositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism to convert concerns into formal decision-making processes when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications (Article 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines notifications as acts to notify administrative agencies of given matters (excluding applications) as may be expressly obligated by laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must treat notifications required by law appropriately and ensure procedures for receipt and processing are clear and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Principles for the Establishment of Administrative Orders (Article 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets general principles for establishing Administrative Orders; public participation and procedural safeguards are emphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as the foundation for public comment requirements and transparency obligations when agencies create Administrative Orders, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Comment Procedures — Implementation Requirement (Article 39)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organs Establishing Administrative Orders, etc. shall, in establishing Administrative Orders, etc., implement procedures for public comment (public notice of the proposed Orders, a 30-day minimum submission period, provision of the proposed text and grounds, and methods for public participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 39 details the duty to publish proposed Orders and grounds, provide the text, ensure at least 30-day comment period (subject to exceptions), and make proposals available by appropriate means (see Article 45 for electronic means).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Provisions for Shortened Comment Periods (Article 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where compelling grounds exist for not setting the 30-day minimum, Organs may set shorter periods but must show grounds at time of public notice; committees that have implemented an equivalent procedure may obviate public comment requirement in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited flexibility for expedited rulemaking but requires disclosure of the reasons for shorter periods and recognizes committee-equivalent procedures as alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making Public the Implementation of Public Comment Procedures (Article 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: When implementing public comment, Organs should, where necessary, endeavor to make public the implementation and provide information relating to the implementation of the procedures for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages transparency about how comment procedures were run (e.g., notices, timelines, venues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Submitted Comments (Article 42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organs Establishing Administrative Orders, etc. must adequately consider all comments submitted within the period for submission of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates substantive consideration of comments (not merely perfunctory treatment); adequacy is required and later public notice must reflect results/changes (Article 43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notice of Results (Article 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of promulgation (or decision not to promulgate), Organs must make public: title of the Administrative Orders, date of public notice of the proposed Orders, submitted comments (or statement of none), and results after considering comments (including differences between proposed and established Orders and grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may in some cases publish a summary of comments first and then publish full comments at the office; may redact or exclude comments where third-party interests would be harmed or other justifiable grounds exist; when no procedures were implemented, agencies must publish title/purpose and reasons for not implementing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Mutatis Mutandis (Article 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions concerning the consideration and publication of comments apply mutatis mutandis to cases where committees have implemented equivalent procedures or where public comment was not implemented under certain Article 40 exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures similar transparency and consideration requirements when alternate (committee-equivalent) procedures are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of Public Notice (Article 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice required by Articles 39 and 43 (and related mutatis mutandis provisions) is to be provided by means using an electronic data processing system or other information and communications technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates use of electronic/ICT means for public notices and delegates necessary matters concerning public notice to the Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures by Local Public Entities (Article 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local public entities must endeavor to take necessary measures to advance guarantee of fairness and transparency in administrative operations consistent with the purpose of this Act, regarding procedures to which the Act is made inapplicable by other provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages subnational bodies to align with Act's fairness/transparency goals even where formal applicability is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary/Transitional Provisions (effective dates and transitional measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies effective dates, transitional rules preserving prior laws for certain procedures or matters until this Act comes into effect, and empowers Cabinet Orders to prescribe necessary transitional measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives temporal rules for implementation and clarifies which prior procedural regimes continue to govern during transition; relevant when assessing whether the Act's procedural rules applied at particular times.
